Deep Autumn vs Deep Winter

Deep Autumn and Deep Winter are neighbouring colour seasons. They share the same depth. The difference is undertone: Deep Autumn is warm-neutral, Deep Winter is cool-neutral; contrast: Deep Autumn is medium-high, Deep Winter is high; chroma: Deep Autumn is medium, Deep Winter is clear.

Questions

What is the difference between Deep Autumn and Deep Winter?

Deep Autumn and Deep Winter are neighbouring colour seasons. They share the same depth. The difference is undertone: Deep Autumn is warm-neutral, Deep Winter is cool-neutral; contrast: Deep Autumn is medium-high, Deep Winter is high; chroma: Deep Autumn is medium, Deep Winter is clear.

Can I be between Deep Autumn and Deep Winter?

Yes. Neighbouring seasons share a lot, and many people sit near the border. That's why Season Card shows your closest season and a runner-up.

How do I tell if I'm Deep Autumn or Deep Winter?

Focus on undertone and contrast and chroma. In daylight, compare a colour from each palette under your chin, for example burnt coral (Deep Autumn) and ice grey (Deep Winter), and see which makes your skin look more even.
